notes.title: Advertising and promotions managers
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as managers increasingly utilize artificial intelligence (AI) tools to test, modify, and oversee ad campaigns, allowing fewer managers to oversee more staff.

notes.title: Claims adjusters, examiners, and investigators
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as computer software and artificial intelligence (AI) will make claims adjustment processes more efficient, allowing adjusters to focus on more complex claims.

notes.title: Insurance appraisers, auto damage
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as specialized software and artificial intelligence (AI) make the appraisal process more efficient, allowing appraisers to focus on more complex claims.

notes.title: Training and development specialists
notes.note: Demand change - share increases as demand for continuous training increases due to accelerating technological advancements such as artificial intelligence (AI) in the labor market.

notes.title: Credit analysts
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as companies increase the productivity of credit analysts by using more data and machine learning in the credit risk analyses process.

notes.title: Information security analysts
notes.note: Demand change, productivity change - share increases as firms increase their IT security staffs and capabilities as a response to increasing threats of cyberattacks aimed at sensitive or financial data, offset slightly by efficiencies gained through increased use of automated and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies to improve security measures.

notes.title: Computer and information research scientists
notes.note: Demand change - share increases as demand for solutions to complex computing challenges and for developing new technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), will support an increased demand for computer and information research scientists.

notes.title: Computer user support specialists
notes.note: Sourcing change, capital/labor substitution - share decreases as more businesses offshore their computer user support or solve computer troubleshooting needs using generative artificial intelligence (AI).

notes.title: Network and computer systems administrators
notes.note: Occupational substitution, productivity change - share decreases as job duties are increasingly performed by DevOps engineers and similar roles, including software developers, and as workers increasingly use third-party automation tools or artificial intelligence (AI) to automate routine tasks.

notes.title: Computer programmers
notes.note: Productivity change, occupational substitution - share decreases as computer programming tasks are more commonly performed by other computer occupations, such as software developers. Computer programming work also continues to be automated, including with artificial intelligence (AI), allowing computer programmers to become more efficient.

notes.title: Software quality assurance analysts and testers
notes.note: Occupational substitution, capital/labor substitution - share decreases as some tasks move to software developers as companies increasingly integrate their testing into their software development processes, and as some testing tasks are automated by artificial intelligence (AI).

notes.title: Web developers
notes.note: Occupational substitution, capital/labor substitution - share decreases as low- and no-code tools, along with artificial intelligence (AI), increasingly automate web development and increasingly allow other workers to complete web development tasks.

notes.title: Web and digital interface designers
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as improvements in design tools, including improvements in design capabilities of generative artificial intelligence (AI), enhance productivity of these workers.

notes.title: Paralegals and legal assistants
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as tasks such as conducting research and preparing documents are increasingly automated via technology including artificial intelligence (AI), reducing the need for these workers.

notes.title: Tutors
notes.note: Capital/labor substitution - share decreases as online tools and digital tutors utilizing generative artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities reduce demand for tutors.

notes.title: Fine artists, including painters, sculptors, and illustrators
notes.note: Capital/labor substitution - share decreases as more images are generated by artificial intelligence (AI) tools, substituting for some illustrators.

notes.title: Special effects artists and animators
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as more animation and post-production tasks are accelerated by the use of technology, including generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools.

notes.title: Graphic designers
notes.note: Productivity change, capital/labor substitution - share decreases as new technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), replace some workers and make other workers more efficient.

notes.title: Actors
notes.note: Demand change, capital/labor substitution - share decreases as fewer domestic television, movies, and live theater are produced and as artificial intelligence (AI) reduces the number of commercial advertising opportunities otherwise available to actors.

notes.title: Broadcast announcers and radio disc jockeys
notes.note: Demand change, capital/labor substitution - share decreases as demand for announcers and on-air talent decreases as radio stations consolidate locations or opt for a DJ-free format. Increased adoption of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated voice technology is expected to further reduce the need for announcers and DJs.

notes.title: Broadcast announcers and radio disc jockeys
notes.industry: Media streaming distribution services, social networks, and other media networks and content providers
notes.note: Demand change, capital/labor substitution - share decreases as demand for announcers and on-air talent decreases as radio stations consolidate locations or opt for a DJ-free format. Increased adoption of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated voice technology is expected to further reduce the need for announcers and DJs.

notes.title: Public relations specialists
notes.note: Productivity change, capital/labor substitution - share decreases as public relations specialists increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) tools for social media content. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is also increasingly used in public relations to produce some content on its own, requiring less involvement of public relations specialists.

notes.title: Technical writers
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools grows, allowing technical writers to produce documentation more efficiently.

notes.title: Writers and authors
notes.note: Capital/labor substitution - share decreases as more written works are generated by artificial intelligence (AI) tools, substituting for some writers.

notes.title: Court reporters and simultaneous captioners
notes.note: Capital/labor substitution - share decreases as simultaneous captioning is increasingly done by artificial intelligence (AI), especially for video content.

notes.title: Broadcast technicians
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as technology including artificial intelligence (AI) allow technicians to perform more activities onsite and in remote locations.

notes.title: Sound engineering technicians
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as the use of wireless technology and artificial intelligence (AI) systems allow technicians to perform tasks more efficiently.

notes.title: Sound engineering technicians
notes.note: Demand change, productivity change - share decreases as technologies such as digital audio workstations allow more artists to produce their own recordings, while wireless technology and artificial intelligence (AI) systems allow technicians to perform tasks more efficiently.

notes.title: Lighting technicians
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as technology, including artificial intelligence (AI) systems, allows workers to design and operate lighting displays.

notes.title: Photographers
notes.note: Capital/labor substitution - share decreases as more images are generated by artificial intelligence (AI) tools, substituting for some photographers.

notes.title: Radiologists
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly adopted in clinical practice, making the radiologist workflow more efficient.

notes.title: Radiologists
notes.industry: General medical and surgical hospitals; private
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly adopted in clinical practice, making the radiologist workflow more efficient.

notes.title: Medical records specialists
notes.note: Demand change, productivity change - share increases as the demand for health care services and complexity of medical coding grow. This demand for medical records specialists will be partially offset by the use of artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools that make the medical coding process more efficient.

notes.title: Medical transcriptionists
notes.note: Capital/labor substitution - share decreases as automation of the medical transcription process by artificial intelligence (AI) tools reduces the need for medical transcriptionists.

notes.title: Insurance sales agents
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly integrated into workflows, allowing insurance sales agents to focus on direct sales activity.

notes.title: Travel agents
notes.note: Demand change, productivity change - share decreases as consumer use of online booking services reduces the need for travel agents. The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools will also allow travel agents to perform administrative and marketing tasks more efficiently.

notes.title: Sales representatives of services, except advertising, insurance, financial services, and travel
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as generative artificial intelligence (AI) is integrated into the sales process allowing sales representatives to focus on direct sales activity.

notes.title: Sales representatives, wholesale and manufacturing, technical and scientific products
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as generative artificial intelligence (AI) is integrated into the sales process allowing sales representatives to focus on direct sales activity.

notes.title: Sales representatives, wholesale and manufacturing, except technical and scientific products
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as generative artificial intelligence (AI) is integrated into the sales process allowing sales representatives to focus on direct sales activity.

notes.title: Demonstrators and product promoters
notes.industry: Advertising, public relations, and related services
notes.note: Capital/labor substitution - share decreases as generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used for product promotion instead of workers.

notes.title: Models
notes.note: Capital/labor substitution - share decreases as the use of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated models grows, reducing the need for models.

notes.title: Sales engineers
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly integrated into workflows, allowing sales engineers to focus on direct sales activity.

notes.title: Customer service representatives
notes.note: Capital/labor substitution - share decreases as advances in speech and language processing and in artificial intelligence (AI) allow computers to handle customer service interactions with greater frequency.

notes.title: Hotel, motel, and resort desk clerks
notes.note: Capital/labor substitution - share decreases as artificial intelligence (AI) software is increasingly used to assist guests with routine enquiries, and self-service kiosks and mobile applications allow guests to complete check-ins and check-outs without a clerk present.

notes.title: Receptionists and information clerks
notes.note: Capital/labor substitution - share decreases as companies use computer software, enhanced with artificial intelligence (AI) technology, to automate data collection, document preparation, and other tasks performed by clerks.

notes.title: Executive secretaries and executive administrative assistants
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as firms increase the use of computer software, enhanced with artificial intelligence (AI) technology, to automate routine back-office functions, such as document preparation.

notes.title: Legal secretaries and administrative assistants
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as firms increase the use of computer software, enhanced with artificial intelligence (AI) technology, to automate routine back-office functions, such as document preparation.

notes.title: Medical secretaries and administrative assistants
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as the increasing use of technology, including artificial intelligence (AI) tools, allows medical secretaries and administrative assistants to perform tasks more efficiently.

notes.title: Secretaries and administrative assistants, except legal, medical, and executive
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as technology, including artificial intelligence (AI) systems, assists workers with routine back office functions, such as preparing documents, scheduling, and notetaking.

notes.title: Data entry keyers
notes.note: Capital/labor substitution - share decreases as organizations increasingly manage, store, and analyze large quantities of data, requiring traditional data entry methods to be replaced by automated processes through use of expanded technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), mobile data capture, and optical character recognition (OCR).

notes.title: Word processors and typists
notes.note: Occupational substitution, capital/labor substitution - share decreases as other workers assume the functions of typists due to the ubiquity of typing skills and traditional typing methods continue to be replaced by automated processes through use of machine learning (ML) technologies.

notes.title: Insurance claims and policy processing clerks
notes.industry: Direct health and medical insurance carriers
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as firms increase the use of computer software, enhanced with artificial intelligence (AI) technology, to automate claims and policy processing.

notes.title: Insurance claims and policy processing clerks
notes.industry: Direct insurance (except life, health, and medical) carriers
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as firms increase the use of computer software, enhanced with artificial intelligence (AI) technology, to automate claims and policy processing.

notes.title: Insurance claims and policy processing clerks
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as firms increase the use of computer software, enhanced with artificial intelligence (AI) technology, to automate claims and policy processing.

notes.title: Insurance claims and policy processing clerks
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as firms increase the use of computer software, enhanced with artificial intelligence (AI) technology, to automate claims and policy processing.

notes.title: Office clerks, general
notes.note: Productivity change - share decreases as increased use of technology, such as artificial intelligence (AI) and electronic filing systems, automate some clerical functions and reduce the need for individuals to perform these duties.
